x: A hearty welcome to Bob Couillaut who was just pipped into 4th place in the Triple Jump with 41'2¼". He is also in his first year as a senior.

Lyle Moar and Bob Couillaut both scored in the Triple Jump, in which Fred Alsop(Hornchurch) was only 2nd, and Laurie O'Hara ran his best ever 1500m in finishing 3rd to Maxwell(Woodford) and Blakesley(LCAT); as did Adrian Major in 8th position.
The best event Belgravewise in this good standard meeting at the Metropolitan Police ground was the Triple Jump in which Bob Couillaut and Lyle Moar finished 2nd and 4th with some terrific jumping.
In the Long Jump, John Mitchell was forced to take 2nd place behind Kelly (HHH) with Bob Couillaut 4th and Barry Townsend 6th, only 1'7" covering the first six competitors.
Bob Jones made it a double by winning the Triple Jump from Bob Couillaut and Barry Townsend was an inch too good for Derek Wade in the high jump.
Bob Couillaut, in the 'A' event, cleared 43'0" for 2nd place whilst R.Bennett broke the sand at a promising 42'7" for 3rd place amongst the 'B' competitors.
John Roberts (SLH) beat Adrian Major in the mile but only by 0.9secs. and Bob Couillaut leapt to 21'6" in the Long Jump, improving by over a foot.
The Triple Jump saw a rare defeat for Bob Couillaut by fellow club man Barry Townsend who cleared his previous best by over a foot. There were no fewer than six Bels. competing in this event.
Bob Couillaut and Lyle Moar filled first two places in the Hop, Step and Jump, held yet again into the wind. These two should both be heading for 45 feet with a little more help from the weather.
